 Inox Wind Q2 Revenue Rises 21%, Profit Declines 43% Amid Commodity Cost Pressures
 Inox Wind stated that the impact on margins seen this quarter was due to commodity and raw material price inflation on account of the West Asia war, creating temporary cost headwinds across the supply chain.
 Chitrika Grover 
 15 Nov 2026 12:22 IST
 Follow Us
 Inox Wind Limited reported revenue from operations of ₹1,354.30 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), registering a 21.01% year-on-year (YoY) increase from ₹1,119.18 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) basis, revenue rose 66.36% from ₹814.10 crore in Q1 FY27. 
 Advertisment However,  Inox Wind's Profit After Tax (PAT) declined 43.17% YoY to ₹68.55 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹120.62 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, PAT increased 6.96% from ₹64.09 crore in Q1 FY27. For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Inox Wind reported a PAT of ₹141.35 crore, down 35.15% from ₹217.97 crore in H1 FY26. 
 Advertisment According to its investor presentation , Inox Wind has pivoted towards equipment sales, with its cash flows beginning to deliver the desired results. Highlighting the progress, the company stated, “We are seeing signs of revenue growth as well as a reduction in debtor days.” 
 Commodity Price Inflation Adds to Margin Pressures 
 In its investor presentation, Inox Wind attributed the margin pressure during the quarter to rising commodity and raw material prices amid the West Asia conflict. The company stated, “Impact on margins seen this quarter due to commodity and raw material price inflation on account of the West Asia war, creating temporary cost headwinds across the supply chain – Incremental contracts and fresh bids being priced dynamically to reflect the current commodity and cost environment, which should help normalize our margin profile as these newer orders move into execution” 
 Advertisment Reported EBITDA Does Not Reflect the Full Picture: Inox Wind 
 In its investor presentation, Inox Wind stated that the reported EBITDA for the quarter does not reflect the full picture, as income from the Wind World O&M portfolio has not been recognised in the profit and loss (P&L) statement for the quarter. The company explained that, had this income been recognised, its consolidated EBITDA margin would have been approximately 20%. 
 As of October 2026, Inox Wind had a well-diversified order book of approximately 3.8 GW, comprising orders from independent power producers (IPPs), public sector undertakings (PSUs), commercial and industrial (C&I) customers, and retail customers. 
 Advertisment The company said its order book provides revenue visibility of more than 24 months, with additional multi-year order visibility from its group IPP platform. Its customer portfolio includes NTPC, CESC, NLC India, Aditya Birla, Amplus/Gentari, Hero Future Energies and Inox Clean, among others. 
 Advertisment During Q2 FY27, Inox Wind secured orders aggregating 350 MW from PSUs and IPPs. Additionally, Inox Green successfully raised ₹300 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) during the quarter. 
 Wind World O&M Portfolio Acquisition 
 Inox Wind also highlighted the completion of payment for the transfer of Wind World India Limited (formerly Enercon India)'s 4.5 GW wind operations and maintenance (O&M) business through the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) process. The payment was made through Inox Green's subsidiary, Vibhav Energy Private Limited (VEPL), pursuant to the Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) executed between VEPL and Wind World India Limited. Its l ine-by-line financial consolidation of the acquired business is expected to begin from Q3 FY27. 
 The company described the transaction as one of the most significant deals in India's renewable energy O&M sector. It expects the acquisition to be value-accretive, with significant scope to improve operational efficiencies through enhanced service offerings, price optimisation and cost optimisation. 
 Inox Wind also stated that the automatic listing of IRSL on the stock exchanges is expected following the receipt of all statutory approvals. The Information Memorandum (IM) has been filed with the stock exchanges.
